transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Ever since a friend from my choir passed away so suddenly, I just haven’t felt like myself. I cry over little things, like the potluck lists, and phone calls I used to handle easily get me all worked up. I’ve even started missing church planning meetings, which I never used to do.
How long ago did your friend pass away, and how long have you been feeling this way since then?
It’s been about a month now—since my close friend from choir died. I’ve been feeling this way ever since.
Over this past month, have you been feeling sad or down, or have you lost interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy, nearly every day for most of the day?
I’m not sure I’d say it’s nearly every day, most of the day. I do get sad, especially when something reminds me of her, but it comes and goes.
Besides feeling sad, have you also been feeling unusually nervous, worried, or on edge since your friend's passing?
Yes, I have. Things that used to be simple, like making phone calls, get me all worked up now. I just don’t feel like myself since she died.
How often would you say you feel this nervous or on-edge feeling—does it happen most days, or only in certain situations like when you have to make a call or attend a meeting?

It’s happening more than just with calls. I get worked up over things I used to handle easily, and I’ve even been missing church planning things I never would’ve missed before. Ever since she died, I just haven’t felt like myself.
Would you say the anxious, on-edge feelings and the sad, tearful feelings are both equally present for you, or does one of them stand out as more prominent than the other?

I think they’re both there. I get tearful over little things, like the potluck lists, and then I get all worked up about making calls I used to handle easily. Since she passed, I just haven’t been myself.
Aside from feeling tearful, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like choir or church events?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t thought of it that way.
Since your friend passed, have you found yourself no longer enjoying or looking forward to choir practice or church events the way you used to?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m enjoying them less or not.
Over the past month, would you say you feel sad or down more days than not, even when nothing specific reminds you of her?
I’m not sure I could say more days than not. I know I get sad when something brings her to mind, but I haven’t really kept track of how often it’s there otherwise.

Would you say these feelings—whether the tearfulness or the nervousness—are making it hard for you to keep up with your usual responsibilities, like work, home tasks, or your relationships with family and friends?
Yes. I’ve had to let other people at church take over the calls, the lists, and parts of the luncheon. I’m just not keeping up with those things the way I always did before.
Along with feeling nervous or on edge, have you noticed physical signs like your muscles feeling tense, your heart racing, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed those kinds of physical things specifically.
Over the past month, would you say you've felt nervous or on edge more days than not, even when nothing specific triggers it?
I don’t know that I could say it’s more days than not. It seems to come and go, and I haven’t really noticed it being there for no reason.
